findings.title: LCQ1: Improving online bank account opening

rendered_html: 📔 Regulatory Bulletin — 22 October 2026 (Daily) Executive Summary • 🟡 Remote account opening: The Government reports existing HKMA supervisory expectations for identity verification, control enhancement and post-opening monitoring, while first-phase iAM Smart step-up-authentication testing begins. No new rule or rollout date is announced; Digital Onboarding and Fraud Operations should prepare evidence of applicable controls and monitor any risk-based expansion. Hong Kong 🟡 Improving online bank account opening 🇭🇰 Item ID: item-20261021-fstb-c441e1accb ⏰ Deadline: No source deadline stated Products: Digital onboarding, SME onboarding The Financial Services and the Treasury Bureau’s Legislative Council reply reports that HKMA already expects appropriate identity-verification and risk-management measures for remote account opening, with systems and controls continuously enhanced. It says banks must effectively identify and verify customers and, after account opening, conduct ongoing due diligence and transaction monitoring, reporting suspicious transactions to law-enforcement agencies. The reply cites 2023 guidance to use clear on-screen messages explaining that selfies or liveness tests are for account opening, and describes in-app authentication and facial recognition for mobile-device binding as existing HKMA-required measures. First-phase testing of iAM Smart step-up authentication for remote account opening has commenced; HKMA will assess security, stability and customer experience before any risk-based expansion, so the timing and scope remain open. Source: LCQ1: Improving online bank account opening Mainland/GBA No validated developments in this run. SG/UK/GLOBAL Benchmark Comparable overseas developments and commercial/control benchmarks. They do not establish Hong Kong requirements. No validated benchmark developments in this run. Watch List • Monitor the outcome and scope of HKMA’s assessment of iAM Smart step-up-authentication testing, including whether it expands to other business areas on a risk-based approach.
